rows.text: RFQ IV.B.2 controls the adopted edition. Basis retained for this module: LRFD 10th Edition (2024), FDOT Structures Manual (January 2026), and project amendments. No newer ACI edition is substituted.
LRFD 5.6.3, 5.6.7, 5.7, 5.10.2, 5.10.3, 5.10.6 and 5.10.8: distributed RC wall checks. FDOT SDG 1.4.2, 1.4.4 and 3.10 modify the cover, durability and service-detailing basis.

LRFD 5.8.2.4 and 5.13: hanger/anchorage basis. The fully embedded fin is not treated as a prequalified ACI base-plate shear lug. The adopted hanger reduction factor is conservatively lower than the verified LRFD reinforced-concrete STM tie factor.

LRFD 6.5.4.2, 6.12.2.2.7 and 6.13.5.3: rectangular fin-plate resistance. The additional elastic combined-stress limit is a deliberately conservative project screen, not a quoted LRFD interaction equation.

Fin geometry, one-row layout, elastic reaction model, nominal-yield development target, and tolerances are declared design assumptions. Approval of the complete local hanger/concrete/saddle/pipe mechanism remains a release condition.

items.name: C006Box3

rows.text: Bridge gravity is not assigned to this wall. Wall gravity passes through its reinforced collection regions, hairpins and bearing saddles into the fin plates and piles. No bond or friction between the pipe and wall is credited for vertical resistance.

Out-of-plane wind is assigned to concrete-to-pipe contact distributed over the wall height, not concentrated at the upper fin row. Fin out-of-plane loading from forced compatibility is not silently included as zero measured demand.
The source wall is conservatively weighed gross, without subtracting pipe volumes. The source weight, cap dimensions, pile layout, existing FBMP loads and unrelated calculations are not changed.

The six-support solution is an elastic demand-distribution model, not proof of gravity load collection in the deep wall. Local strut/node design, hanger-to-wall load collection and imposed pile movement remain explicit completion items.

Fin plates are checked for their actual factored reaction and the full nominal yield of their designated two-hairpin group. Nominal yield is not multiplied by the DC load factor and is not claimed to represent actual simultaneous yielding in all fins.

rows.text: All six fins are in one upper row. There is no equal-sharing assumption between multiple vertical rows. Additional rows require a new distribution model.

The computed wall-bottom offset from terrain is retained and shown above. It is not silently repaired by changing the source wall height. Confirm whether the intended wall extends to or below grade.

The selected round saddle is additional steel, not the fin plate itself. Its positive bearing fit, lateral restraint, local contact behavior and any attachment weld are required details to be completed separately.

rows.text: REQUIRED LOCAL DETAIL — NOT A SHARP-EDGE HANGER

Two inverted-U #5 hairpins wrap a round steel bearing saddle above each fin. Hairpins are normal to the fin plane; the fin lies between their legs. Use a fitted bearing seat and positive saddle retention. Do not weld the reinforcing bars.

The tail-length and steel-area checks above are completed. The local saddle bearing/contact, concrete load collection into those tails and local strut/node confinement must still establish the assumed load path; they are not certified by the area-times-yield calculation.
General face-grid bars are not included in the designated hairpin yield target. Additional connected bars that can impose force on the fin require updating the interface demand.

rows.text: Provide the selected face grid in both directions at each broad face, with horizontal bars outermost. Continue the face grids around ends and edges using developed returns or compatible laps; do not cut bars off merely because they meet a pipe.

Provide two designated #5 hairpins at every fin; no credit from the distributed grid is included in the fin-development target. Additional local concrete splitting/strut reinforcement is subject to the local node design.

Drive and survey piles before fabricating/installing final fins and reinforcement. The selected wall fit requires the position envelope shown above, including the transverse direction; the current cap tolerance cannot be substituted unchecked.
Forms/falsework carry wet concrete until the concrete and anchorage have the required strength. The completed embedded bearing mechanism is not assumed available in fresh concrete.

No collision or seismic exemption is newly certified here. Retain the established project applicability decisions only after confirming the governing geometry and classification. Construction, fatigue, and differential-pile-movement effects outside the assigned loads remain coordination items.

items.name: C006Box240

rows.text: LOCAL WELD HANDOFF AXES AND REFERENCE
O is the midheight of the nominal full-height fin root at the pipe tangent plane. Local +x points outward along that fin, +z points downward, and +y is chosen so x cross y = z (right-handed).

Fz is positive downward. A downward load at positive x creates negative My. A positive transverse offset creates positive Mx. Reversing the transverse offset reverses Mx; the paired rows below are complete concurrent cases.

For opposite-facing fins, the local axes rotate with the fin. Transform each complete case to the weld program axes. If the actual weld-group centroid differs from O, relocate once using Mnew = Mold + r cross F.

Fx, Fy and Mz are zero in the assigned vertical hanger model, not measured zero compatibility actions. Wall-wind reactions enter the piles through the separate distributed contact path. Any force assigned to the fin by a revised model must be added as a complete load case.

Actual Service I and Strength I/III rows are load demands. HY+ and HY- are nominal-hairpin-yield development targets and must not be multiplied by the DC or wind factors again. They are not asserted to occur simultaneously at every fin.

rows.text: EXPLICIT COMPLETION ITEMS — NOT INCLUDED IN AN OVERALL PASS

1. Local node and wall gravity collection: substantiate the reserved transfer zone, actual struts/nodes, splitting confinement, bar development beyond the relevant separation surfaces, and the round saddle contact/retention detail.

2. Receiving pipe: check localized shell yielding/plastification, punching/tearing and interaction with the actual concurrent pile stress state at the fin elevation. Use the effective pipe wall, not the nominal 5/8-inch wall. No pipe local-resistance pass is claimed here.
3. Geometry: confirm source wall-bottom elevation, environmental cover and the tighter wall-region position tolerance. The old source wall quantity has not been silently changed.
4. Weld: use the exported root cases in the separate weld calculation, including relocation to the actual weld centroid and adjacent base-metal failure paths. No weld design is contained in C006.

5. Preserve external applicability decisions for collision, seismic, construction and fatigue; resolve differential pile movement/cap-wall restraint consistently with the full substructure model. The one-foot wind strip is not a coupled pier model.
